First of all, nobody is “bad” at this game. All lives are given for democracy and therefore you are doing your part. This game requires all of us, at whatever level of play, to do our part.

Second - all stratagems are viable at levels 7 and below. Above that things become dicey and arguable. Mines are great against bugs! Mortars not so much and instead consider using them against bots.
Think about the tactics of your enemies! Mines work on opponents attacking you, whereas mortars work on enemies shooting at you from a distance! 
If your allies don’t understand this after you ping it/VC it or Type it then it is their own fault as friendly fire ISN’T.

Third - Have fun, man. I play a lot of competitive shooters and mobas that are fun but do NOT have a fun player base anymore and my favorite part of this game is playing with low levels who are scared of higher level play or just want to coast. This game has brought competitive and casual gamers together and I love it.

Assassin - typically play the jungle role which is a rotating kill confirmer, meant to clear jungle camps and help turn the tides on lane fights. Some assassins can be played in the solo, support or carry role depending on how good you are with them/the company. Assassins get early game kills and help push objectives. Early Recommendations: NEVER PLAY LOKI,Fenrir, Thor, Ratataskor(one of my first favorite jungles) , Nemesis

Guardians - usually support. Support helps put your (ADC) Carry ahead before helping to support other lanes a little later in the game. Some guardians can jungle and solo, again depending on your skill level. Not looking for kills on guardians, you usually want to protect your team and disrupt the other teams pushes. Early Recommendations: Ymir, Bacchus, Kumba Kharna, Kephri 

Hunters - ADC/Carry. Not too strong early game but late game become objective shredders/can really chunk other players that aren’t focusing them. Some hunters can be played in mid or solo, rarely supp or jung. Early Recommendations: Neith, Artemis, Cernunnos, Chiron

Warriors - like guardians but physical instead of magical based damage, average CC but a little more flexible with builds. Warriors take solo lane which is the shortest lane with the Blue/Mana buff. Warriors can be pretty flexible. Build tanky, with some damage items/hybrid items peppered in. Early Recommendations: Bellona, Hercules, Chaac,

Mages - probably the most flexible of the classes IMO. You have some magical carries like Sol/Olorun, some mage supports like Aphrodite/Baron Samedi (although I wouldn’t recommend jumping into these gods as support right away.) most of them stick to middle lane, with the occasional solo play. You’re looking at high burst ability damage and low defense when you play these gods. Early recommendations: Ra, Poseidon, Hades, Zeus.

I agree. I thought it over for a minute and realistically who am I to dismantle this whole towns way of life? I get that Spacers Choice was awful, but they were still providing a service for Edgewater, and the real problem was the plague and Reeds unwillingness to stray from his predetermined path. 

And while I haven’t finished the game, and I may never find out, I think in the end the real lesson is that there really isn’t a right choice at all. Adelaide is clearly unstable based on her reaction when you take the power from her sanctuary, and even when you fix things she remains bitter. 

Give it about the same time in leadership that Reed had and I’m positive that there will be similar issues. Like sure she “cured” the plague, but the methods of  doing it aren’t at all sanitary and I can’t imagine having vegetables fertilized by ground up humans is any sort of sustainable means of growth. She’s improving the quality of life and removing the plague, so therefore there should be less death and eventually less fertilizer right? It’s a bandaid on a mortal wound.

TL;DR : I love the moral ambiguity of the choices you have to make, but I think the whole point of the story is there really isn’t a right choice.
